luna_probability.hypothesis_a: The small 2/12 denominator overestimated the baseline; this is the primary explanation.
luna_probability.hypothesis_b: Dated-snapshot/provider drift cannot be excluded because stationarity was not pinned.

local_breakout.issue: The secondary acceptance sheet maps run_stop.status=completed to incomplete assurance even though run_stop, summary, and campaign metadata agree on full.

incidents.harvest: A timestamp-bearing build and then target-directory-specific Mach-O bytes made binary identity a measured variable. build.rs was made deterministic and preflight now fails closed on the declared binary SHA before spend.

A point estimate from 2/12 was incorrectly treated as a known population rate and a narrow count range was called a prediction band. Declarations now require denominator, confidence interval, and a Beta-binomial predictive band.

adjudicator_corrections.before: point-p binomial band without baseline denominator or interval
adjudicator_corrections.after: denominator plus confidence interval plus Beta-binomial predictive band

go: Keep earned-only run-end selection with a fixed, predeclared N.
Use BoN as opportunity amplification for configurations with observed full support; at pooled Luna p-hat=4/42, the N=6 point amplification is about 45.1%.
Retain all candidates and publish Oracle@N, Selector@N, Selection gap, and diversity.
no_go: Do not use the original 17% point estimate or promise a 70% success rate.
Do not apply BoN as a universal remedy to the Gemma locked-failure configuration.
Do not enable predictive pruning, mid-run selection, repair connection, or population-level quality claims.
requirements: Every series must pin revision, suite SHA, binary SHA, model identifier, baseline denominator, confidence interval, and Beta-binomial predictive band before spend.
Any dated provider snapshot must be preferred when discoverable; otherwise the alias and stationarity limitation must be explicit.
Reconcile the acceptance-sheet assurance projection before using that sheet as an independent selector input.
Keep correlation and quality claims descriptive until their predeclared denominators are large enough.
